recipes.name: Cilantro Lime Rice
recipes.blurb: One of the most-used recipes in the whole book. Pairs with carne asada, chicken bowls, burrito bowls, fajitas.
steps: Rinse rice in a strainer under cold water, stirring with your fingers, until the water runs mostly clear.
Add rice, water, butter, and salt to the saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Don't walk away.
Once boiling, cover, drop heat to LOW, and cook 15 minutes — lid stays on the whole time.
Turn the heat off and let it rest, still covered, 10 minutes.
Add lime juice and cilantro, fluff with a fork, and serve.

recipes.name: Pico de Gallo
steps: Dice the tomatoes and onion small. Chop the cilantro.
Combine in a bowl.
Add lime juice and salt, mix.
Rest 15 minutes, then taste and adjust salt.

recipes.name: Blender Salsa
recipes.blurb: The everyday salsa you'll make constantly.
steps: Put everything in the blender.
Blend 10–15 seconds — do not overblend, you want texture.
Taste, add salt if needed, refrigerate.

recipes.name: Salsa Roja (Taco-Shop Style)
steps: Roast tomatoes, jalapeños, garlic and onion under the broiler or in a dry skillet until charred.
Blend with salt until smooth.
Cool and serve.

recipes.name: Salsa Verde
steps: Roast tomatillos, jalapeños, garlic and onion until soft and blistered.
Blend with cilantro and salt.
Taste and adjust.

recipes.name: Guacamole
steps: Mash the avocados to the texture you like.
Add lime, onion, cilantro and salt.
Mix, taste, adjust salt.

recipes.name: Ground Beef Taco Meat
recipes.blurb: One of the highest-value recipes in the book — taco night, burrito bowls, nachos.
steps: Heat the skillet over medium.
Add beef and break it apart as it browns.
Drain excess grease if needed.
Add the spices and water; cook 3–4 minutes until saucy.
Serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Fajita Bowls
steps: Slice peppers and onion; trim the chicken.
Toss everything together with oil and seasoning.
Spread on a sheet pan and roast at 425°F for 25 minutes, until chicken hits 175°F.
Build the bowl: rice, chicken, peppers, pico, guacamole.

recipes.name: Slow Cooker Salsa Chicken
recipes.blurb: One of the best set-and-forget meal-prep recipes there is.
steps: Put everything in the crockpot.
Cook LOW 6–8 hours or HIGH 3–4 hours.
Shred with two forks, stir back into the sauce, serve.

recipes.name: Authentic Carne Asada
recipes.blurb: The crown jewel. Learn this and you'll impress people.
steps: Mix all marinade ingredients, add the steak, and marinate at least 4 hours (overnight is best).
Remove the steak and pat it completely dry — this is what lets it sear instead of steam.
Heat the skillet over medium-high with avocado oil.
Sear 4–6 minutes per side to an internal 130–135°F.
Rest 10 minutes. Do not skip this.
Slice thin AGAINST the grain and serve.

recipes.name: Breakfast Burritos
recipes.blurb: Meal-prep king. Make a batch, freeze, grab on the way out.
steps: Cook the sausage, then remove.
Scramble the eggs.
Combine sausage, eggs and cheese.
Fill tortillas, roll, and wrap each in foil or plastic. Freeze.

recipes.name: Barbacoa-Style Beef (Dutch Oven)
steps: Season the roast and brown it on all sides, then remove.
Cook the onion 5 minutes.
Add broth and spices; return the beef.
Cover and cook at 325°F for 4 hours.
Shred, stir back into the juices, serve.

recipes.name: Restaurant-Style Meat Sauce
recipes.blurb: Your foundation. Master this first — it feeds spaghetti, baked ziti, lasagna, meatball subs.
steps: Heat the Dutch oven over medium with the oil.
Cook the onion 5–7 minutes until soft, not browned.
Add garlic, cook 30 seconds.
Add beef, brown completely, breaking it apart.
Add tomatoes, salt, pepper, Italian seasoning and sugar.
Simmer at least 45 minutes — 90 is better. Taste and adjust salt.

recipes.name: Perfect Spaghetti Night
steps: Boil heavily salted water — it should taste slightly salty.
Cook spaghetti 8–10 minutes.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain (don't rinse).
Add the spaghetti straight into the sauce, toss, loosen with pasta water if needed, serve.

recipes.name: Homemade Meatballs
steps: Mix everything gently — don't overwork it or they get tough.
Form golf-ball-sized meatballs.
Bake at 400°F for 20 minutes, to an internal 160°F.
Add to sauce and simmer 15 minutes.

recipes.name: Garlic Bread
steps: Mix the butter, garlic, parsley and salt.
Spread on the bread.
Bake at 375°F for 10 minutes.
Broil 1–2 minutes — watch it closely so it doesn't burn.

recipes.name: Chicken Parmesan Bowl
steps: Pound the chicken to even thickness.
Egg wash, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Bake at 425°F for 20–25 minutes to 165°F.
Top with sauce and mozzarella, broil 2 minutes.
Serve over pasta.

recipes.name: Italian Sausage & Peppers
steps: Cook the sausage over medium 12–15 minutes, then remove.
Cook the peppers and onion ~10 minutes.
Slice the sausage, return it to the pan, serve.

recipes.name: Creamy Garlic Chicken Pasta
steps: Cook the pasta, reserving some pasta water.
Cook the chicken to 165°F and slice.
Melt butter, cook garlic 30 seconds.
Add cream, simmer.
Whisk in parmesan.
Add pasta and chicken, loosen with pasta water, serve.

recipes.name: Baked Ziti
steps: Cook the pasta but undercook by 2 minutes.
Mix pasta with sauce, transfer to a baking dish.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 375°F for 25 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Dutch Oven Lasagna Pasta
recipes.blurb: All the flavor of lasagna, half the work.
steps: Brown the beef, add onion, cook.
Add sauce, dry pasta and enough water to cover.
Simmer until the pasta is tender.
Top with cheese, bake at 375°F for 15 minutes.

recipes.name: Homemade Pizza Night
recipes.blurb: Pizza sauce needs no cooking — just stir it together.
ingredients: Pizza sauce: 1 can crushed tomatoes + 1 tsp salt + 1 tsp garlic powder + 1 tsp oregano
steps: Preheat the oven as hot as it goes (500°F) for 45 minutes — use a steel or stone if you have one.
Stretch the dough.
Add sauce, then cheese, then toppings.
Bake 10–14 minutes until blistered.
Rest 3 minutes, slice.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Chicken Bowls
recipes.blurb: One of the highest-value meal-prep recipes in the entire book.
ingredients: Sauce: ½ cup soy sauce, ¼ cup water, 2 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 cloves garlic, 1 tsp grated ginger
steps: Cook the rice.
Air fry the chicken at 400°F for 20 minutes to 175°F.
Simmer all sauce ingredients (not the slurry) 5 minutes.
Stir in the slurry, whisk, let it thicken.
Slice the chicken, coat in sauce, serve over rice with broccoli.

recipes.name: Beef & Broccoli
ingredients: Sauce: ⅓ cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tsp sesame oil, 3 cloves garlic, 1 tsp ginger
steps: Freeze the steak 20 minutes, then slice thin against the grain.
Cook the broccoli first, then remove.
Cook the beef over high heat ~2 minutes.
Add sauce, return broccoli, toss, serve.

recipes.name: Fried Rice
recipes.blurb: Cold, day-old rice is the secret. Plan ahead.
steps: Cold rice only — fresh rice turns to mush.
Scramble the eggs, then remove.
Cook the vegetables.
Add the rice and break it apart.
Add soy sauce, then the eggs.
Finish with green onions.

recipes.name: Garlic Soy Chicken
steps: Marinate 30 minutes.
Air fry at 400°F for 20 minutes to 175°F.
Serve.

recipes.name: Egg Roll Bowl
recipes.blurb: All the flavor of an egg roll, none of the wrapping.
steps: Brown the pork.
Add garlic and ginger.
Add the slaw mix, cook until softened.
Add soy sauce, serve.

recipes.name: Orange Chicken (Air Fryer)
ingredients: Sauce: ½ cup orange juice, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp honey, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp ginger
steps: Bread the chicken (egg, then flour).
Air fry at 400°F for 20 minutes.
Simmer the sauce until slightly thick.
Toss the chicken in sauce, serve.

recipes.name: Sesame Broccoli
steps: Roast the broccoli at 425°F for 20 minutes.
Finish with soy sauce and sesame oil.

recipes.name: Chicken Stir Fry
recipes.blurb: The 'clean out the fridge' recipe.
ingredients: Sauce: ¼ cup soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 garlic clove
steps: Cook the chicken, then remove.
Cook the vegetables.
Add sauce, return chicken, toss, serve.

recipes.name: Japanese-Style Steak Rice Bowl
ingredients: Sauce: 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp butter, 1 tsp garlic
steps: Cook the steak to 130–135°F.
Rest, then slice thin.
Serve over rice with the sauce and green onions.

recipes.name: Korean Ground Beef Bowls
recipes.blurb: One of the best meal-prep recipes ever — 15 minutes, start to finish.
steps: Brown the beef and drain.
Add soy, brown sugar, garlic and ginger.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Serve over rice with green onions.

recipes.name: Chicken Katsu
steps: Bread the chicken: flour, egg, then panko.
Air fry at 400°F for 18–20 minutes.
Slice and serve.

recipes.name: Potsticker Bowl
steps: Cook the pork.
Add the vegetables.
Add the sauce.
Serve over rice.

recipes.name: Ultimate Beef Chili
recipes.blurb: Your signature meal-prep recipe. Add 1 tbsp cocoa + 1 tsp espresso powder for a 'why is this so good' version.
steps: Brown the beef in the Dutch oven 8–10 minutes, then drain the grease.
Add the onion, cook 5 minutes.
Add garlic, cook 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, beans, tomato paste, broth and seasonings.
Bring to a simmer, reduce heat, and cook 1–2 hours — longer is better.
Taste and adjust salt.

recipes.name: Slow Cooked Pot Roast
recipes.blurb: One of the best Sunday meals — and it makes the apartment smell incredible.
steps: Season and brown the roast on all sides, then remove.
Cook the onions.
Add broth, return the roast, add the vegetables.
Cover and cook at 325°F for 4 hours, until it shreds (205°F+).
Shred and serve.

recipes.name: Air Fryer Chicken Thighs
recipes.blurb: A cornerstone recipe. The backbone of a hundred meal-prep bowls.
steps: Mix the seasonings and coat the chicken.
Air fry at 400°F for 18–22 minutes to 175°F.
Rest 5 minutes.

recipes.name: Crispy Breakfast Potatoes
steps: Dice the potatoes.
Boil 5 minutes, then drain (this is the trick to crispy).
Season.
Bake at 425°F for 35 minutes.

recipes.name: Egg Sandwich (Master)
recipes.blurb: This single recipe will save you hundreds of dollars in drive-thru breakfasts.
steps: Toast the muffin.
Cook the eggs.
Add cheese, assemble.

recipes.name: Smash Burgers
recipes.blurb: Learn this and you'll stop buying burgers.
steps: Make 4 oz balls.
Get the skillet very hot.
Smash a ball flat, cook 2 minutes.
Flip, cook 1 minute, add cheese.
Serve.

recipes.name: BBQ Pulled Chicken
steps: Slow cooker, LOW 6 hours.
Shred, mix with sauce, serve.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Sausage & Vegetables
steps: Spread everything on a sheet pan.
Roast at 425°F for 25 minutes.

recipes.name: Loaded Baked Potato Bowls
steps: Bake the potatoes at 425°F for 60 minutes.
Split and top with everything.
Serve.

recipes.name: Homemade Mac & Cheese
steps: Make a roux: melt butter, whisk in flour.
Add milk slowly, whisking.
Stir in the cheese until smooth.
Fold in the cooked pasta, serve.

recipes.name: Chicken & Rice Meal Prep
recipes.blurb: The bodybuilding classic. Simple, cheap, hits your protein.
steps: Cook all three.
Portion into containers.

recipes.name: Beef & Potato Skillet
steps: Cook the potatoes first.
Add the beef, then the onion.
Season and serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Noodle Soup
steps: Cook the vegetables.
Add the broth and chicken.
Simmer.
Add the noodles last so they don't go mushy.

recipes.name: Dutch Oven Beef Stew
recipes.blurb: Cold-weather champion.
steps: Brown the meat.
Add vegetables and broth.
Bake at 325°F for 3 hours.

recipes.name: Homemade Meatloaf
steps: Mix everything.
Form a loaf.
Bake at 350°F for 60 minutes to 160°F.

recipes.name: High Protein Breakfast Burritos
steps: Cook the turkey sausage.
Scramble the eggs.
Combine, fill the tortillas, wrap and freeze.

recipes.name: Steak & Sweet Potato Bowls
steps: Cook the steak to 130–135°F, rest, slice.
Roast the sweet potato and broccoli.
Assemble the bowl.

recipes.name: Air Fryer Salmon
recipes.blurb: One of the healthiest, fastest recipes in the book.
steps: Coat the salmon in oil and seasoning.
Air fry at 400°F for 8–10 minutes to 125–130°F internal.

recipes.name: Greek Chicken Bowls
steps: Cook the chicken.
Build the bowl with rice, chopped cucumber and tomato.
Top with tzatziki.

recipes.name: Buffalo Chicken Bowls
steps: Cook the chicken and toss in buffalo sauce.
Build the bowl with rice and broccoli.
Drizzle with Greek yogurt ranch.

recipes.name: White Chicken Chili
steps: Combine everything in a pot.
Simmer 1 hour.
Shred the chicken back in, serve.

recipes.name: Protein French Toast
steps: Whisk eggs, protein powder, cinnamon and milk.
Dip the bread.
Cook on a buttered skillet over medium until golden both sides.

recipes.name: California Burrito
recipes.blurb: The San Diego icon. Skip the tortilla and bowl it for the lighter version.
steps: Make the carne asada and fries.
Pile carne asada, fries and cheese on the tortilla.
Roll tight and serve.

recipes.name: Carne Asada Fries
steps: Make the fries and carne asada.
Layer fries, cheese (melt it), carne asada.
Top with guacamole and pico.

recipes.name: Fish Tacos
steps: Season and pan-cook or air-fry the fish.
Warm the tortillas.
Build with cabbage, fish and lime crema.

recipes.name: Fish Taco Bowls
steps: Cook the fish.
Build the bowl with rice, cabbage, pico.
Top with chipotle sauce and a squeeze of lime.

recipes.name: Rolled Tacos (Taquitos)
steps: Fill tortillas with shredded beef, roll tight.
Air fry or pan-fry until crisp.
Top with cheese and lettuce.

recipes.name: Master Pizza Dough
recipes.blurb: The recipe to memorize. Freezes great — make 4 batches and thaw 24 hrs in the fridge for pizza anytime.
steps: Combine water and yeast, wait 5 minutes.
Add flour, salt and oil.
Knead in the KitchenAid on speed 2 for 8 minutes (or 8 min by hand).
Move to an oiled bowl, cover, rise 1–2 hours until doubled.
Divide into 2 balls, rest 30 minutes.
Stretch, top and bake. Preheat the oven 500°F for 45 minutes; use a steel if you have one.

recipes.name: Dutch Oven No-Knead Bread
recipes.blurb: The recipe that makes you realize: I can actually make bread.
steps: Mix to a shaggy dough.
Cover and rise overnight, 12–18 hours.
Preheat the Dutch oven at 450°F.
Bake covered 30 minutes, then uncovered 15 minutes.
Cool completely before slicing.

recipes.name: Dutch Oven Sandwich Bread
steps: Mix, then knead 8 minutes.
Rise 1 hour.
Shape into a loaf, rise 45 minutes.
Bake at 375°F for 35 minutes to an internal 200°F.

recipes.name: Hamburger Buns
steps: Mix and knead to a smooth dough.
Rise until doubled.
Shape into buns, rise again.
Bake at 375°F for 15–18 minutes.

recipes.name: Dinner Rolls
steps: Mix and knead.
Rise until doubled.
Shape into rolls, rise again.
Bake at 375°F for 15 minutes.

recipes.name: Buttermilk Biscuits
steps: Mix the dry ingredients.
Cut in the cold butter (cold is the whole game).
Add buttermilk, fold gently.
Cut biscuits, bake at 425°F for 12–15 minutes.

recipes.name: Brownies
steps: Mix everything.
Pour into a pan.
Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes.
Cool, then slice.

recipes.name: Homemade Cinnamon Rolls
recipes.blurb: KitchenAid showcase — people remember homemade cinnamon rolls.
ingredients: Dough: 500g (4 cups) flour, 1 cup warm milk (110°F), 2¼ tsp instant yeast, ⅓ cup sugar, ⅓ cup melted butter, 2 eggs, 1 tsp salt
Filling: ½ cup softened butter, 1 cup brown sugar, 2 tbsp cinnamon
Icing: 4 oz cream cheese, ¼ cup butter, 1 cup powdered sugar, 1 tsp vanilla
steps: Stir the warm milk and yeast together, wait 5 minutes until foamy.
In the KitchenAid with the dough hook, combine flour, sugar, melted butter, eggs, salt and the yeast mix; knead 6–8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and rise 1–1.5 hours until doubled.
Roll into a 16×12" rectangle. Spread with soft butter, then sprinkle the brown sugar and cinnamon.
Roll up tightly from the long edge and cut into 12.
Place in a greased 9×13 pan and rise 30–45 minutes.
Bake at 350°F for 22–28 minutes until golden.
Beat the icing smooth and spread over the warm rolls.

recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Cookies
steps: Cream the butter and both sugars 2–3 minutes until light and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt separately, then mix into the wet.
Fold in the chips.
Chill the dough 30 minutes (optional but worth it).
Scoop golf-ball portions onto a lined sheet, spaced apart.
Bake at 375°F for 10–12 minutes — pull when edges are golden and centers still look soft.
Cool 5 minutes on the pan before moving.

recipes.name: Focaccia Bread
steps: Mix flour, water, salt, yeast and 2 tbsp oil into a wet, shaggy dough.
Cover; over the first hour do 3 rounds of stretch-and-fold with wet hands.
Rise 1–2 hours until puffy, or refrigerate overnight for deeper flavor.
Pour 2–3 tbsp oil onto a sheet pan and stretch the dough to fill it.
Rise 45 minutes.
Dimple all over with oiled fingers, drizzle more oil, scatter rosemary and flaky salt.
Bake at 450°F for 20–25 minutes until deep golden.

recipes.name: New York Cheesecake
recipes.blurb: Cool slowly, don't rush — that's how you avoid cracks.
ingredients: Crust: 1½ cups graham cracker crumbs, ¼ cup sugar, 6 tbsp melted butter
Filling: 4 blocks (8 oz each) cream cheese at room temp, 1¼ cups sugar, ½ cup sour cream, 2 tsp vanilla, 4 eggs
steps: Mix the crust, press firmly into a 9" springform, bake at 350°F for 10 minutes.
Beat the cream cheese smooth, then beat in the sugar, then the sour cream and vanilla.
Add the eggs one at a time on LOW speed — don't overbeat or it cracks.
Pour over the crust.
Set the pan in a foil-wrapped water bath and bake at 325°F for 60–75 minutes until edges set and center still jiggles slightly.
Turn the oven off, crack the door, cool inside 1 hour.
Refrigerate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight.

recipes.name: Reverse Seared Ribeye
recipes.blurb: The steak recipe. Impressiveness: 5/5. Serve with Caesar salad and Dutch oven bread.
steps: Salt the steaks and leave them uncovered in the fridge 12–24 hours.
Bake at 250°F until they hit 115°F internal (about 30–45 minutes).
Heat the skillet very hot with avocado oil.
Sear 60 seconds per side.
Add butter, garlic and rosemary; baste.
Pull at 130–135°F, rest 10 minutes.

recipes.name: Braised Short Ribs
recipes.blurb: Special-occasion food.
steps: Brown the ribs on all sides.
Cook the vegetables.
Add wine and reduce.
Add broth, return the ribs.
Bake at 325°F for 3.5 hours.
Serve over mashed potatoes.

recipes.name: Restaurant-Style Caesar Salad
ingredients: Dressing: ½ cup mayo, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 garlic clove, 2 tbsp parmesan, anchovy optional
steps: Whisk the dressing ingredients.
Toss with chopped romaine.
Top with croutons and parmesan.

recipes.name: Holiday Mashed Potatoes
steps: Boil the potatoes until fork-tender.
Mash with butter.
Add warm milk gradually — cold milk ruins the texture.
Salt to taste.

recipes.name: Smoked-Style Pulled Pork (Dutch Oven)
recipes.blurb: For people without a smoker — your Dutch oven gets you most of the way.
ingredients: Dry rub (salt, pepper, paprika, garlic, brown sugar)
steps: Coat the pork in the rub.
Brown it, add a splash of broth.
Cover and cook at 275°F for 6–8 hours until it shreds.
Shred and serve.

recipes.name: Carne Asada Party Pack
ingredients: 5 lbs carne asada (scale the marinade x2.5)
steps: Marinate the steak overnight.
Cook in batches so the pan stays hot.
Set everything out as a build-your-own taco bar.

recipes.name: Prime Rib
recipes.blurb: Holiday centerpiece. Serve with mashed potatoes and horseradish.
ingredients: 1 bone-in prime rib roast (4–5 lbs / 3–4 bones)
steps: 1–2 days ahead, pat the roast dry and rub all over with the salt. Refrigerate uncovered (dry brine).
Pull it out 2–3 hours before cooking to come to room temp.
Mix the butter, garlic, herbs and pepper; coat the roast all over.
Roast at 250°F until the internal temp is 10°F below your target — about 3–4 hours for medium rare.
Rest 20–30 minutes, loosely tented with foil.
Crank the oven to 500°F and return the roast 8–10 minutes to brown the crust.
Slice between the bones and serve. Doneness (pull 10°F early): rare 120°F, medium rare 130°F, medium 140°F.

recipes.name: Thanksgiving Turkey
recipes.blurb: Use a thermometer, never guess.
ingredients: ¼ cup kosher salt + 1 tbsp baking powder (mixed)
steps: 1–2 days ahead, pat the turkey very dry and rub the salt mix all over, including under the breast skin. Refrigerate uncovered.
Day of: pull it out 1 hour before and pat dry again.
Rub butter under and over the skin; stuff the cavity with onion, lemon and herbs.
Roast at 325°F, about 13 minutes per pound, until the breast reads 157°F and thighs 165°F (~3 hours for a 13-lb bird). Tent with foil if browning too fast.
Rest 30–45 minutes — the temp carries up to a safe 165°F.
Carve.
